Triage: multi-org semantics of platform/system tables → `domain:services`, type Task, `pm:blocked`.

`Blocked-by:` #11303

Rationale: **#11303 is the ruled parent of this question and is in flight** — the maintainer has already ruled its messaging-table instances (sys_inbox_message / sys_notification / sys_email), verbatim from the batch record: 「…应该写 organization_id」. The messaging half of this card's list is therefore answered by inheritance and being implemented there. What remains genuinely open is the tail (logs / config tables, where platform-scoped-by-design is a defensible answer). Unlock action: when #11303 lands, re-scope this card to the residual tables only, measured against the landed write-side pattern — the residue is either a mechanical extension of that pattern or a short decision list, and it should not be guessed before the pattern exists.

## What is already answered — ⛔ do not re-open, and do not re-measure it

Triage's unlock (`11611#issuecomment-5435274081`) re-scoped this card when #11303 closed. **The messaging half of the body's inventory is answered by inheritance**: the maintainer ruled those tables carry `organization_id` (verbatim 「…应该写 organization_id」, recorded on #11303) and the write-side pattern has **landed** there.

⇒ Inbox messages & receipts / notifications & deliveries / email / templates — **1,300 rows — are out of scope.** ⛔ Do not re-litigate, do not re-measure, do not include them in your answer except as "already ruled and implemented".

## What this card now asks — the residual tail only

- **Logs family** — job logs, audit logs, feed, automation runs (**8,044 rows**)
- **Config & metadata misc** — capabilities / metadata / files / permission sets / positions etc. (**233 rows**)

**Measure each residual table against the LANDED #11303 write-side pattern first.** Find that pattern in the tree before forming any opinion — it is the reference every per-table answer is measured against.

Per table, the answer is one of exactly two things:
1. a **mechanical extension** of the landed pattern, or
2. an entry on a **short decision list for the maintainer**.

⛔ **"Platform-scoped by design" is a defensible answer for logs and config, and it must not be guessed.** A log row that is deliberately global is not a defect; asserting it is one would be worse than leaving the question open.

## ⚠️ The fence — where "mechanical extension" stops being yours to write

The reporter has **8,044 existing rows** on a production install. So:

- If a residual table is a mechanical extension of the landed pattern **and carries no implication for existing rows** — new rows start carrying the column exactly as #11303 does, old rows stay as they are — implementing it is in scope.
- ⛔ If it implies **backfilling or migrating existing rows**, that is existing-data-migration shape and is **maintainer floor**. Put it on the decision list and **stop** — do not write it, and do not write a migration "ready for review".
- ⛔ If it is a genuine design choice (should audit logs be org-scoped at all?), that is the decision list too.

⚠️ Check what #11303 actually did about existing rows before you classify anything, and say so in the report. If the landed pattern itself backfilled, the fence moves and I want to know that rather than have you infer around it.

## ⭐ The deliverable is a written answer, not a diff

This is a **customer asking for design intent**, not a bug report — their own words: *"We are not reporting a malfunction — everything works. We only need the design intent confirmed, and to know whether org markers will be added later."*

⇒ ⛔ **Do not close this card, and do not consider it done, without stating the answer on it**: per residual family, is the absence of `organization_id` by design or pending, and on what reading. A PR with no written answer fails this card even if every gate is green. `premise_still_valid: false` with **no PR and a written measurement** is a perfectly good delivery here — possibly the most likely one.

Write it so the reporter can act on it operationally, which is what they asked for.

## Verification

- Whatever suites cover what you touch — and if you touch nothing, say so plainly rather than reporting a vacuous green.
- Gate union from `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` on your **actual** changed set (possibly empty); exit codes captured **before** any pipe. `PREREQUISITE NOT MET` is **NOT MEASURED**, not red.
- **Changeset**: only if you ship something. ⛔ Never an empty changeset; a measurement-only delivery needs no changeset and should say so.
- ⛔ No model names in any pushed artifact.

## Report

Post your terminal JSON report as a comment on **this issue first**, then return it. Leave **your own** claim comment before starting — the assignee here is the PM session, not you. Include as named fields: the landed #11303 pattern you measured against, the per-table verdict for each residual family, and the decision list if any.

⚠️ Reach GitHub with the **MCP tools** (`mcp__github__issue_read` / `add_issue_comment` / `create_pull_request`, schemas via ToolSearch). Raw REST / `curl` / `gh` is **403 from a dev seat by design** and is never a reason to stop.

## Answer — design intent for the residual platform tables

Measured on `main` at `366f89576`. **No code was changed**; the reasoning is below and the machine-readable report follows in the next comment. The messaging half of your inventory (1,300 rows) is already ruled and repaired at the producers on #11303 and is not re-litigated here.

---

### 1. A correction first, and it comes from your own data

The body says these are tables where **100% of rows (old and new)** lack `organization_id`. For two of the four log tables that is not the shape you have — and your own concurrent scan on #11303 (same install, same day, 2026-08-23) is the evidence:

| Table | total rows (#11303) | NULL rows (#11303) | figure listed on this card |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `sys_audit_log` | 4,485 | 1,510 (34%) | 1,510 |
| `sys_activity` | 3,469 | 916 (26%) | 916 |

The numbers in this card's inventory are **NULL-row counts, not table populations**. Audit logs are already **66% stamped** on your install and the activity feed **74% stamped**. So the accurate statement is not "logs never carry an organization" — it is "some log rows had no organization in scope at write time". That distinction *is* the answer for those two tables, and it is the reason the 8,044 figure should not be read as "8,044 rows that are missing something".

⇒ **Please re-run the config & metadata group as total-vs-NULL per table.** For `sys_permission_set` and `sys_position` that single number is what separates "working as designed" from a real symptom — see §4.

---

### 2. The mechanism — why the column's presence tells you nothing

Four facts, all of them in the shipped code, that together answer "by design or gap?" for any platform table:

1. **The column is blanket-injected, not authored.** `SchemaRegistry.applySystemFields({ multiTenant })` adds `organization_id` to *every* object under a multi-org posture unless the object opts out. That is why your scan found 112 org-column-bearing tables. Exactly **two** platform objects opt out today (`sys_api_key`, `sys_sso_provider`), so for everything else the column's presence is provisioning, not a declaration of intent. The pin on `sys_job` says it plainly: such an object is *"tenant-scoped only incidentally — `organization_id` is kernel-injected, never authored."*
2. **The value comes from the acting execution context.** The engine stamps from `execCtx.tenantId` on insert. Three sanctioned platform-row writers (audit, approvals, automation runs) go further and resolve the **subject record's own** organization first, using the actor only as fallback (#8287 / #8707 / #10101, one shared resolver in `@objectstack/metadata-core`).
3. **A producer with no organization in scope writes NULL, on purpose.** Anything running under a bare system context (`isSystem: true`, no tenant) has no organization to thread, and the standing ruling on your #11303 is **never fabricate one**. Verbatim from the merged fix: *"a wrong organization_id is worse than a null — a null is visibly missing, a wrong value is silently authoritative."*
4. **NULL is a named bucket, not a missing value.** The SQL driver materializes the organization key part as `COALESCE(organization_id, '__global__')`, and ADR-0120 D3/S8 records the reading: *"NULL rows form one platform bucket, unique among themselves … the 'NULL = the platform tenant' reading the write path already uses."*

And the load-bearing one for your question — the engine's own refusal for org-less system writes **deliberately does not fire on the `sys_` namespace**, because (quoting the module) *"their rows are deliberately global / cross-organization: this is #8672's reasoning ('an org-less row is defensible for `sys_permission_set`'), which the #8844 ruling confirms holds for platform objects and does NOT generalize to application objects."*

**So: an org-less row on a `sys_` table is a ruled, defensible state.** That is the口径 you asked for. What is *not* uniformly true is that each table has **declared** it — that gap is §6.

---

### 3. Logs family — the 8,044

| Family | Object | Verdict | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|
| Job logs — 5,613 | `sys_job_run` | **By design.** No organization exists to record. | Sole writer `DbJobAdapter` runs under a constant system context with zero organization handling. Its parent `sys_job` is explicitly deployment-global (`unique: 'global'`, pinned): *"the job catalogue is a property of the deployment, not of an organization"*, and the `job` metadata type is closed to tenants on all three flags (`allowOrgOverride: false` — "no per-org job fork"). A scheduled tick fires because a cron expression matched, not because an organization acted. |
| Audit logs — 1,510 | `sys_audit_log` | **Already answered — ruled accepted 2026-08-24.** Not a gap. | All three writers (CRUD, auth-event, read-audit) already stamp through the shared resolver. The residual NULLs are writes where no organization was resolvable at all (system context, no session organization, or a subject with no organization column). The alternative — deriving one on the single-tenant branch — was considered and **not taken**. |
| Feed — 916 | `sys_activity` | **Same ruling, same reading.** | As above. 74% of your feed rows already carry an organization. |
| Automation runs — 5 | `sys_automation_run` | **Already implemented.** Writer stamps; NULL is meaningful. | Both row families (terminal history and live paused rows) stamp `organization_id` from the trigger record's own organization, falling back to the acting tenant. A NULL means specifically: *a plain scheduled sweep, which has no single subject* — and fabricating an acting organization there stays vetoed. |

**Will org markers be added to job logs later?** The product question behind it is answered, and answered "no, not opened": ADR-0126 §5 states that plumbing an organization into schedule / time-relative / api trigger types is *"not opened; it is a product question ('which org does a nightly sweep belong to'), not a plumbing one."* Only record-change-triggered work carries an organization by construction.

---

### 4. Config & metadata misc — the 233

| Item | Object | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Capabilities | `sys_capability` | **By design, and load-bearing — must not be stamped.** The platform's own rows live in the NULL-organization bucket *by definition*: the ownership test that tells a platform capability apart from an org admin's own authored copy of the same name is literally `managed_by = 'platform' AND organization_id IS NULL`. Stamping those rows would destroy that discrimination and let an organization's authored copy be overwritten by the platform's. |
| Metadata | `sys_metadata_activation` | **By design today, and explicitly planned to change later** — this is the one table where "will markers be added?" has a published answer. ADR-0126 §5: *"Install-level rows now. Every row is written with `organization_id` NULL"*, and the column is *"reserved — the per-org dimension is an additive column later, never a redesign"*, pre-charted narrowly to record-change-triggered flows *"when a real multi-org customer asks"*. The field's own description in the schema says the same: NULL on every row this line writes, no writer sets it yet. |
| Permission sets, Positions | `sys_permission_set`, `sys_position` | **Mixed, ruled, and already repaired forward in the release you are running.** These declare `unique: 'organization'` and were formerly seeded organization-less; that was ruled *invalid state under a walled posture* and repaired in **17.2.0** (#10103): the four seeders now upsert by `(name, organization_id)`, one pass per organization, and also fire on organization creation. Pre-fix rows are **deliberately never reaped** — grants point at them by row id, so deleting them would revoke standing access with no signal. Separately and permanently, `bootstrapPlatformAdmin` writes organization-less `sys_permission_set` rows on **every** boot, and the 2026-08-20 ruling keeps it that way because the platform-admin grant points at the `admin_full_access` row by id. |
| Files | `sys_file` | ⚠️ **The one genuine open question on this card.** See §6. |

⚠️ **Actionable for you, on permission sets and positions.** On 17.2.0 under a walled posture your catalog should contain **both** your organization's own copies *and* the organization-less rows. If your scan really shows 100% NULL there rather than a NULL subset, that is a symptom worth reporting separately. The platform already tells you which class each org-less row belongs to: at boot it emits a named warning distinguishing `platform-bucket` (*"no action is required"*, and re-initializing does not clear them) from `pre-fix-residue`. **Check your boot log for those two lines** — they are the intended operational signal and they name the remedy.

---

### 5. Operational guidance — what to do with this

- **Do not backfill, and do not touch platform tables.** Your instinct was right and remains right. Forward-stamping only is the standing posture; existing rows stay as they are unless a maintainer separately orders otherwise. A one-off repair sweep does exist in the platform for approvals and automation runs, but it is maintainer-ordered, dry-run-first, and never something a project runs on its own.
- **Do not write reports or cleanup scripts that filter platform tables by organization.** This is the real operational hazard, and it is the one your inventory is pointing at. A NULL `organization_id` on a `sys_` table means "the platform bucket", not "unclassified data" — an `organization_id = :org` predicate over `sys_audit_log` silently drops a third of your audit trail, and over `sys_capability` it drops the platform's entire capability catalog.
- **For the log families, scope by what the row is *about*, not by the row's own column.** `sys_audit_log`, `sys_activity` and `sys_automation_run` all carry the subject's object and record id; those are the reliable dimension for a per-organization report, and they are populated on rows whose own organization column is NULL.
- **Expect the mixed state to persist and to be correct.** It is not a migration in progress.

---

### 6. What is genuinely still open — one item, escalated, not guessed

**`sys_file` never carries an organization on any install, and unlike every other table above there is no reading under which that is clearly intended.**

Measured: `StorageMetadataStore.createFile` calls `engine.insert('sys_file', full)` with **no execution context at all**. The two callers are HTTP upload routes that *do* hold an authenticated session — they read `session?.userId` for `owner_id` on the very same call — so an organization is in scope and simply is not threaded. That is structurally identical to the #11303 headline finding, where one un-passed argument put four tables at 100% NULL.

But it is **not** in the "clearly by design" set either: `sys_file` is deliberately excluded from the telemetry/plumbing class (audit keeps auditing it precisely because those rows are *"mostly permanent business truth"*), it declares no tenancy opt-out, and its sibling `sys_attachment` — same subsystem, written through the ordinary data API — does not appear in your org-less inventory at all. One carries an organization, the other never does.

It is being escalated rather than fixed here because stamping it **changes read visibility**: under a walled posture the strict Layer 0 predicate annihilates the driver's NULL-compatibility arm, so newly stamped files become organization-walled while your 233 existing rows do not — a mixed population with a behavioural blast radius on reads. That is a design call, not a mechanical extension, and this card's own analysis names "some tables carry it, some don't" as the most dangerous outcome. It needs a maintainer ruling first.

## `sys_file` — ruled a gap, now fixed, **with a backfill**

The ruling was option **A with backfill**: `sys_file` should carry `organization_id`, and the rows that never got it are repaired rather than left behind. Landed in PR #12929.

Two halves:

1. **Forward** — the upload path now threads the acting session's active organization into the insert, so new files are stamped. If a request has no active organization, nothing is stamped (unchanged from today) rather than a value being guessed.
2. **Backfill** — a one-off sweep that derives each existing row's organization from the record that holds the file, and stamps it.

## ⚠️ The part that matters for your operations planning

This is why the backfill was made a condition of the fix rather than a nice-to-have, and it applies directly to your install:

On a walled multi-org posture, the tenant predicate the driver builds is NULL-tolerant — `organization_id = :tenant OR organization_id IS NULL` — but the security layer above it AND-composes a **strict** equality over that, and the conjunction is the strict equality alone. The practical consequence:

> Once stamping starts, **`organization_id IS NULL` stops meaning "visible to everyone" and starts meaning "visible to no one."**

Your scan measured `sys_file` at 100% NULL. A forward-only fix would therefore have split that table in two — new files correctly walled, and **every file you have today invisible to every principal**. That is the outcome the backfill exists to prevent, and it is the answer to your original question of whether to account for this in operations: **yes, and the accounting is the backfill, not a filter you write project-side.**

(If any of your installs run the `single` posture, nothing changes for them under any of this — the wall is inert there.)

## What you should plan around: the residual count

The sweep **refuses to guess**. It reads both channels that can hold a file — the exclusive field reference and every `sys_attachment` join row — and stamps a row only when every holder answered and they all answered the *same* organization. Anything else is left NULL and **reported**, never inferred. In particular one holder in an organization sitting beside a holder with none is treated as ambiguous, not as a majority vote, because stamping the answer would simply aim the invisibility at the other holder instead.

So the deliverable you want is the **residual-NULL report**, broken out by reason: no holder, holder not found, holder not organization-scoped, holder has no organization, ambiguous holders, and rows the sweep cannot address. It runs **dry-run by default** and prints that breakdown on the dry run as well as the applied run — which is what makes the dry run a decision document rather than a preview. Each write carries only `{ id, organization_id }`, so nothing else on the row is touched and the undo is exactly "write NULL back to these ids", which the dry run names.

⚠️ Any rows left in that residual set stay invisible under a walled posture. **That count is the thing to look at before you enable anything**, and it is the number worth telling us if it is non-zero and large.
